data.headline: Jack Survives A Bed Bath And Beyond Scare
data.deck: Cook'd needed every last point to hold off BedBathNBIJAN22 in a game that came down to the wire
body: Jack's been living large at 5-1 this year, sitting pretty at rank 2 in the power rankings with an 86.5 shot at the playoffs, and for about three quarters of this one it looked like business as usual. Then John's BedBathNBIJAN22 squad decided to remind everybody why nothing in this league is ever comfortable.

Cook'd put up 112, a number that usually ends a conversation. Instead it nearly started a fistfight. BedBathNBIJAN22 answered with 105.86, close enough that John could taste it, close enough that Jack had to sit there sweating through the whole back half of the slate watching his lead shrink point by agonizing point.

When the dust settled, the margin was 6.14. That's it. That's the whole gap between Jack cruising to 5-1 and John climbing out of the 2-4 hole he's been stuck in all season. The Squeaker trophy has Jack's name on it for a reason, and it is the kind of trophy you don't brag about so much as you just quietly stop sweating.

John's BedBathNBIJAN22 squad has now dropped another close one and sits at 43.7 to make the playoffs, pure Bubble territory, the kind of record where every single one of these six-point nail biters matters. Jack rolls on at 5-1, pointsFor sitting at 685.58, looking every bit the contender while also looking like a man who needs to stop scheduling games this close to his heart rate monitor.

data.headline: Taylor Gets Mercy Killed While Jackson Throws A Party
data.deck: Seven games, one certified bloodbath, and Andrew's heart in a blender yet again. Let's run it all down before the chugs get handed out.
body: Week 6 had a little bit of everything: a blowout for the ages, a nail biter that actually mattered, and Taylor quietly becoming a recurring character in this newsletter for all the wrong reasons.

Ben's Jackson Off held off Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69, 116.72 to 109.82. Andrew put up a number that wins most weeks and still went home with nothing, which at this point should just be his walkout music.

Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher turned Trip's 50 Shades of Zay into a cautionary tale, 121.38 to 94.78, with Christian McCaffrey dropping 30.7 and Malik Nabers chipping in 28.5. That's not a fantasy matchup, that's a mugging with a receipt.

Sean's Burrowed Alive beat Matt's Shough Her Gently 102.78 to 90.72, and yes, 102.78 was enough to win this week, which tells you everything about the state of Shough Her Gently. Matt's sitting at 1-5 and the 0.7 playoff odds say the fat lady isn't singing, she's already in the parking lot.

Adam's First Down Syndrome absolutely ran Taylor's Victorious Secrets off the field, 117.14 to 63.58, a 53.56 point massacre fueled by Germie Bernard's 25.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 25.4. Taylor takes home The Shart again, his second trip to the podium this season, and at this rate the league should just name a chug after him.

Jack's Cook'd needed every last point to hold off John's BedBathNBIJAN22, 112 to 105.86, your Squeaker and Game of the Week rolled into one gorgeous 6.14 point margin. This is what a real fantasy football game is supposed to feel like, and the rest of you should take notes.

And then there's Jackson. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy put a combine on Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried, 130.4 to 73.3, a 57.1 point beatdown that was the Blowout of the week before Bhayshul Tuten's 24.7 even had a chance to matter for Bearcat. Didn't help. Nothing was helping.
Aaron's Romo911 closed out the slate with a 107.6 to 95.02 win over Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, keeping the Bubble crowded and everyone's blood pressure elevated heading into next week.

data.headline: Josef Stacks Two Monsters While Bearcat Burns One for Nothing
data.deck: The individual scoreboard from Week 6, where some guys got paid and others just watched the pyre
body: Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher didn't need the whole roster this week, just two guys going nuclear. Christian McCaffrey dropped 30.7 and Malik Nabers added 28.5, and between the two of them Josef steamrolled Trip's 50 Shades of Zay 121.38 to 94.78 without much resistance.

Speaking of Trip, he wasn't exactly sitting on his hands. Kenneth Walker III put up 27.9 for him, a borderline elite line that still ended in an L because that's just how the math worked out this week. Welcome to fantasy football, where you can have a great Sunday and still lose.

Adam's First Down Syndrome got a two-man wrecking crew of his own, Germie Bernard going for 25.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba chipping in 25.4, both of which helped bury Taylor's Victorious Secrets 117.14 to 63.58. Taylor, you're on the clock for a chug.

And then there's Bearcat. Bhayshul Tuten put together a genuinely strong 24.7 and it meant absolutely nothing, because Hog Tied and Deep Fried still got demolished by nunnells 73.3 to 130.40. A great individual week trapped inside a disaster of a roster. Some men just can't be saved.

data.headline: Week 6 Hardware: Jackson Takes Home Half The Trophy Case
data.deck: The Squirtnite banquet committee hands out its weekly hunks of fake gold, and one man cannot stop winning things that are mostly insults.
body: Gather round the folding table, boys, because it's time to hand out the cursed plastic. Grab a chug, grab a napkin, and let's get to it.

Manager of the Week goes to Jackson of Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, who dropped 130.40 points on the league like he had something to prove on a Tuesday. He did not, he just has a good team and a flair for the theatrical.
The Shart belongs to Taylor of Victorious Secrets, who mustered 63.58 points and will be chugging accordingly. We already covered the wreckage up top. Moving on, because some wounds need air.
Blowout honors also go to Jackson, because apparently one trophy wasn't enough tonight. His 57.10 margin of victory buried bearcat2789 so deep the funeral home called asking for a deposit.

Squeaker goes to Jack of Cook'd, who snuck past BedBathNBIJAN22 by 6.14 points in what was officially the Game of the Week. Nail-biter, heart palpitations, the whole deal. John is still checking his lineup for ghosts.
Lucky Dog is Sean of Burrowed Alive, who won with just 102.78 points, somehow outlasting Matt's Shough Her Gently in a fight nobody wanted to watch but everybody did anyway.

Heartbreaker goes to Andrew of Bibi's Ballers 69, who put up 109.82 points and still lost. That is the fantasy football equivalent of acing the test and failing the class because the teacher didn't like your face.

And finally, Bench Rot, because somebody has to be held accountable for leaving 52.96 points rotting on the pine, and that somebody is, once again, Jackson. Three trophies in one week. Buy the man a shelf, or at least stop letting him talk at the draft.
data.signOff: See you next week for more hardware, more shame, and hopefully a Shart winner who isn't a repeat offender.

data.headline: Jackson Smashes Bearcat, Then Benches His Own Blowout
data.deck: Nunnells drops 130.40 on a 1-5 team and still finds a way to leave points in the garage
body: Jackson put up 130.40 this week, the best number anybody posted in Squirtnite FFL, and he did it by turning Bearcat into a speed bump. Hog tied and deep fried managed 73.30, which means this wasn't a win so much as a public execution with a 57.10 margin attached, officially the Blowout of the week.

Give the man his flowers. This is Jackson's second Manager of the Week nod of the season, and he sits at 5-1 with 798.32 points for, a 97.2 playoff probability, and the top seed in the standings. That's not luck, that's a guy who built a roster that eats 1-5 teams for breakfast.

Here's the undercut: Jackson also led the league in Bench Rot, leaving 52.96 points sitting on his own bench while he was busy torching Bearcat's season. Imagine scoring 130.40 and still managing to strand enough points on your couch to have won this game twice over against literally anyone else. That's not a flex, that's a confession. The guy is so loaded he can misplay his lineup and still lap the field by 57.10.
Enjoy the top seed, Jackson. Just maybe check the bench before next week, your backups are starting to outscore half this league's starters.
data.signOff: Chug something, nobody's safe, see you next week.

data.headline: Power Rankings: Jackson Rules The Roost, Matt Finds The Basement
data.deck: Week 6 in the books, 9 weeks left, 7 playoff spots, and most of this league is already running on fumes and bad decisions.
body: Fourteen teams, one trophy case, and a whole lot of bubble teams lying to themselves about their playoff odds. Here's where everybody stands after Week 6.

1. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson): Dropped 130.40 on Bearcat by 57.10, grabbed Manager of the Week, and still left 52.96 points rotting on the bench. Clinch Watch at 97.2%, start printing the bye week shirts.
2. Cook'd (Jack): Survived a 6.14 point nail-biter over John's BedBathNBIJAN22 in the Game of the Week. Winning ugly works just as well as winning pretty when you're sitting at 86.5%.
3. Jackson Off (Ben): Put up 116.72 to edge Andrew's Bibi's Ballers. Sitting at 84.7% playoff odds while pretending he's not sweating the bubble like everyone else.
4. Romo911 (Aaron): Beat Chase Browns with Downs 107.60 to 95.02, but Aaron's got two Shart trophies sitting in his case like a bad tattoo he can't laser off.
5. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip): Got run over by 26.6 points despite Kenneth Walker III going off for 27.9. Trip's defense watched that one from the parking lot.
6. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff): Dropped 95.02 in the loss, but 72% playoff odds mean Jeff can afford one more bad Tuesday night.

7. First Down Syndrome (Adam): Moved up a spot torching Victorious Secrets 117.14 to 63.58. Germie Bernard and Jaxon Smith-Njigba combined for a stupid amount of production while Adam crawls out of mediocrity.
8. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef): Somehow dropped a spot despite Christian McCaffrey putting up 30.7 and Malik Nabers adding 28.5. Tells you everything about how deep this league actually is.
9. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew): Scored 109.82 and still lost, taking home the Heartbreaker trophy and a 43.3% coin flip at the playoffs.
10. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John): Put up 105.86 in a loss that's going to haunt John's group chat all week. Sitting at 43.7% to sneak in.
11. Burrowed Alive (Sean): Won with just 102.78, the Lucky Dog of the week. At 10.5% playoff odds, that luck needs to show up a few more times.
12. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat): Got smoked 73.30 to 130.40, though Bhayshul Tuten's 24.7 was the one bright spot in an otherwise 1.3% future.

13. Victorious Secrets (Taylor): Posted 63.58, claimed the Shart for the second time, and somehow moved up a spot anyway. The fantasy equivalent of getting promoted after fainting during the presentation.
14. Shough Her Gently (Matt): Fell to Burrowed Alive's lowly 102.78, dropped to dead last, and Matt's 0.7% playoff odds are basically a hospice sentence at this point.
data.signOff: Chug responsibly, Taylor. See everyone next week.

data.headline: Josef Hits the Parlay, Everyone Else Hits the Waiver Wire Panic Button
data.deck: Nabers and McCaffrey turned Zyn-bo Squisher into a cheat code while the rest of the league scrambled for table scraps
body: Josef did not discover fire this week, he just rostered Christian McCaffrey for 30.7 and Malik Nabers for 28.5 and watched 50 Shades of Zay get run over like a stray dog in a cul de sac. 121.38 points. That is not a waiver pickup, that is a hostage situation, and tripnistico never had a chance.

Speaking of guys who needed a body on the waiver wire, Adam's roster of First Down Syndrome quietly stacked Germie Bernard at 25.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 25.4 in the same lineup and still only clipped Taylor's corpse by 53.56. Imagine having that kind of firepower and the margin is the story, not the score. Adam is one week from being annoying about this.
Trip got his own flex out of the deal too, Kenneth Walker III going for 27.9 in a loss that still has 50 Shades of Zay sitting at a 4-2 record and a very real playoff case at 78.0 percent.

And then there is bearcat2789, who found Bhayshul Tuten for 24.7 points in a week his team lost by 57.10 anyway. A great pickup can only do so much when the rest of Hog tied and deep fried is actively deep fried.
data.signOff: Keep scrolling that wire, gentlemen, somebody's RB2 is somebody else's savior.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is A Ghost Town And Everyone Deserves To Be Named
data.deck: Zero trades this week, which says a lot about a league with three teams under 1 percent to make the playoffs and apparently zero urgency about it.
body: I sat here all week with my grading rubric sharpened and nobody gave me a single trade to judge. Not one. Fourteen men, several of them actively drowning, and not a single DM got sent.

Let's be clear about who should have been working the phones. Taylor is sitting at 0.5 percent to make the playoffs after Victorious Secrets put up 63.58 and got annihilated by Adam's First Down Syndrome squad. Matt is at 0.7 percent after Shough Her Gently lost by 12.06 to a Burrowed Alive team that is also 2-4. Bearcat is at 1.3 percent after getting run over by 57.10 points, and he's the one guy on this list who actually had a great performance to sell, Bhayshul Tuten dropped 24.7 on everybody and nobody called to ask about him.

Instead everybody just sat on their hands and let the standings harden into concrete. No grades to hand out this week because there was nothing to grade, which might be the most honest indictment of this league I've written all season. Get off the bench, gentlemen. The trade deadline does not wait for your feelings.
data.signOff: Make a move or make peace with where you're sitting. The SquirtRag will see you next week.

data.headline: Jackson Hosts a Mercy Killing, Taylor Volunteers as Tribute
data.deck: The league's best team gets fed the league's worst team, and somewhere a chug is already being poured preemptively
body: Nunnells sits at 97.2 percent to make the playoffs, just dropped a 130.40 on the field, and now gets to host Victorious Secrets, who have lost five straight and are clinging to a 0.5 percent playoff chance like a toddler clinging to a steak knife. Taylor already owns two Shart trophies this season. There is no version of this preview where I pretend that trend stops here. This is your Shart Bowl, ladies and gentlemen, and the betting line isn't close.

Elsewhere the actual football is pretty good. Jack's Cook'd squad, sitting at 5-1 with an 86.5 percent playoff clip, hosts Aaron's Romo911 crew in a matchup of two teams that both know how to win ugly and win close. Ben's Jackson Off travels to face Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher, a borderline-playoff clash between a team that just mashed the Ballers and a team still riding Christian McCaffrey's 30.70 from last week. Trip's 50 Shades of Zay heads into First Down Syndrome looking to keep pace in a crowded bubble that has basically everyone from seed 3 through seed 10 sweating.

Then there's Bearcat, 1-5 with a 1.3 percent playoff shot, hosting Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs. If Taylor somehow finds a way to avoid the gutter, Bearcat is standing right behind him with a towel.
data.signOff: Drink water, lose anyway. See you Sunday.

data.headline: Taylor's Secrets Are Out and They're All Bad
data.deck: Victorious Secrets puts up 63.58, loses by 53.56, and earns his second Shart like it's a loyalty program
body: Let's talk about Taylor. Let's really sit with Taylor for a minute, because what Victorious Secrets did this week deserves more than a passing mention in a recap nobody reads past the first paragraph.

63.58. That's the number. Write it on a napkin, tattoo it on your forearm, whatever, just make sure it follows you around, because that's what Taylor put up against Adam's First Down Syndrome, who dropped 117.14 on him like it was a parking ticket he didn't even notice getting. Adam got 25.7 out of Germie Bernard and 25.4 out of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, two receivers just absolutely feasting, while Taylor's lineup sat there like a buffet nobody showed up to. The margin was 53.56. That's not a loss, that's a eulogy.

And here's the part that really should hurt: this is the second time this season Taylor has worn the Shart crown. Second time. There is a throne being built for this man and it is made entirely of empty red Solo cups. His points for on the season sits at 505.1, dead last in a 14 team league, and his record is 1-5, which somehow still overstates how competitive Victorious Secrets has been. Playoff odds? 0.5 percent. That's not a bubble team, that's a team currently being dissolved in acid.

Next week Taylor draws nunnells, the league's number 1 power ranking team fresh off 130.40 and a 57.10 blowout, which means Victorious Secrets is about to go from 63.58 to whatever is below 63.58, a number science has not yet invented. There is no bright side here. There is no moral victory. There is only Taylor, alone, holding a controller, wondering why he started the guys he started.

So here it is, the absolute bottom of the barrel, scraped clean, licked dry. Forget the hose, forget the gas station twelve pack sitting warm in your soul, Taylor. Tonight you drive to the stadium itself, climb the fence after hours, find the exact section where First Down Syndrome's 117.14 happened on the scoreboard in your head, and you chug a full pitcher standing on the 50 yard line while security slowly walks toward you and you do not care, because 63.58 point two time Shart champions do not fear mall cops anymore. They fear nothing. They have already lost everything. Chug, bitch.
